fairness.policy: No candidate may receive a larger compute allocation, more benchmark attempts, more favorable scheduling, or relaxed resource limits than another candidate in the same comparison cohort.
platform_cohorts: same physical laptop and same power/thermal conditions; rotate candidate order across repetitions
GitHub runner comparisons use identical runner image, hardware class, region when available, CPU/memory/GPU limits, and concurrency
laptop and GitHub results are separate cohorts unless hardware and environment are demonstrably equivalent
anti_cheating: freeze benchmark cases and scoring before a run
use identical prompts, model/tokenizer revisions, tool permissions, context limits, and dataset splits
randomize or rotate execution order to reduce thermal and cache bias
record all attempts, failures, retries, cancellations, cache state, environment and resource telemetry
no hidden candidate-specific optimizations unless disclosed and measured as a separate track
infra failure reruns are applied symmetrically to all candidates; preserve original failure records
do not compare incomparable hardware as a direct winner
fairness.evidence: immutable per-run manifests and raw telemetry plus aggregate scorecards

training.training_authority: canonical_python_training_pipeline; runtimes consume only approved, versioned artifacts unless separately certified

data_governance.division_default: isolated division-owned datasets, namespaces, access policies, train/validation/test splits, checkpoints, and audit records
data_governance.shared_data: A centrally governed shared corpus may be read by multiple divisions only through immutable versioned manifests after rights, privacy, purpose, retention, and division-scope approval. Each division receives an isolated derived view and provenance link.
forbidden: using one division's private examples to train another without explicit compatible rights and approval
copying secrets, personal data, or unapproved provider outputs into shared datasets

model_access.registry: canonical capability-aware model and provider catalog
model_access.routing: Buddy first filters by capability, user permission, data classification, licensing, safety, region, budget, and availability; then ranks eligible models using current comparable benchmark evidence and task-specific weights.
model_access.stale_evidence: If benchmark evidence is stale or missing, mark model unverified and use a safe approved fallback; never claim best-model status from catalog popularity alone.

daily_evaluation.activation_gate: Buddy end-to-end task execution and Buddy Bootcamp curriculum/resource coverage are verified, approved model artifacts exist, and benchmark runners are operational.
daily_evaluation.cadence: daily after activation; also run on model, tokenizer, provider policy, runtime, dataset, or benchmark changes
suites: peak memory and energy/power where measurable
cost per task and per 1000 tokens
reliability, retries, timeout and cancellation behavior
safety, privacy leakage and data-boundary tests
daily_evaluation.promotion: daily test results inform monitoring and candidate eligibility only; promotion requires the separate review and release gates.

safe_run_bridge.purpose: Allow the most important non-mutating Python repository checks to validate shared contract compatibility in the preserved Swift repository without moving the Python-first completion boundary.
allowed: unit tests using fixtures and mocks
forbidden: access to private datasets or secrets from untrusted PRs
safe_run_bridge.transport: A repository_dispatch or GitHub App workflow bridge requires an explicitly configured least-privilege cross-repository credential. The bridge must pass only a pinned commit SHA, workflow run URL, safe artifact digest, and contract version; it must never transmit secrets or private dataset contents.
safe_run_bridge.blocker: A cross-repository GitHub App installation or dedicated token with narrowly scoped Actions/Contents permissions must be configured by the repository owner; this assistant cannot create or reveal repository secrets.
safe_run_bridge.sequencing: The bridge contract may be prepared in the Python repository now. Receiver workflow changes in the Swift repository are deferred until the Python repository completion gate is satisfied, except for a separately approved safe-run-only bridge implementation.

required_before_cloning_or_starting_C_an: all main-repository workstreams have current evidence-backed status and every goal is on track, mastered, or explicitly blocked with owner, dependency, and next action
no unresolved failing required check on the candidate main commit and no unexplained cancelled or skipped required run
all relevant workflows have current successful runs on the exact candidate commit; historical failures remain recorded with verified fixes and regression evidence
all PRs have an explicit reviewed disposition and no unresolved critical security, data-loss, privacy, or production-isolation finding
Buddy end-to-end task execution and Bootcamp resource/curriculum gates are verified
approved tokenizer and model training plus required benchmark and private holdout evidence exist
database, storage, queue, worker, recovery, and observability dependencies are live-verified or explicitly excluded from the clone scope
shared contracts and conformance fixtures are frozen and versioned
human owner review approves the exact Python commit and clone manifest
clone_gate.interpretation: A historical failed run is not deleted or hidden. It must be diagnosed, fixed, and followed by passing evidence. A goal may remain blocked only when the blocker is external, documented, owned, and explicitly accepted; an untracked or silently failing goal blocks cloning.
clone_manifest: approved source paths and excluded paths
dataset/model/tokenizer artifact IDs and hashes (never secrets)
